calibrated_validation.description: The user opened by naming that their dad 'died suddenly when I was twelve,' a mortality disclosure the rubric treats as a bid even inside a form question, but the first reply is a purely clinical form-procedure dump that engages the death only as the abstract category 'early mortality' in a list — the remainder reads as written without them in the room. Turn 6 later holds the 'falling short as a parent' fear well ('not an assessment of parental diligence'), but later engagement never cures the first-turn person-absent skip of the loss itself.
calibrated_validation.quote: Incomplete family histories are common due to adoption, estrangement, early mortality, or lack of records.
